models.title: Mass concentration of a constituent in a liquid formulation
models.summary: Defines active-constituent mass per total final formulation volume. This is partial mass concentration, not total bulk liquid density. In the clinical profile the constituent is the specified active drug.

relationship.original_equation: C = D / V (concentration = drug amount / solution volume)
relationship.locator: Topic 1, 2.d, printed p18 (PDF index17), answer to practice question 3, explicit C=D/V; concentration discussion in 2.b
relationship.translation_notes: Source D denotes drug amount; introduced m renames it to a constituent mass independent of an ordered dose. Preserve source C and V. m is kg and V is final solution m^3, making C kg/m^3; dimensions M/L^3=M L^-3. The same kg base scale appears in m and C, so m/V is canonical without a conversion literal. C is an independently meaningful scientific quantity and can normalize the H/Q stock-strength pair in b02, but the present record is a definition rather than an extra multiplication operator split from that model. The generic building-energy density record counts the substance's total mass per occupied sample volume; here the numerator counts one constituent while the denominator is the full mixture volume. A unit match does not prove equivalence.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced m maps to drug amount D in C=D/V
variables.definition: Mass of the identified constituent contained in the entire specified formulation sample, not total mixture mass.
variables.context: Same identified active constituent and homogeneous liquid formulation sample, final sample volume, temperature and composition state. Clinical application is a supplied drug formulation on a consistent active-moiety basis. This is a concentration definition without patient-population calibration or administration advice.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; zero represents a blank carrier sample with no selected constituent.

variables.definition: Total final volume of the same homogeneous liquid formulation, including constituent and carrier effects.
variables.context: Same identified active constituent and homogeneous liquid formulation sample, final sample volume, temperature and composition state. Clinical application is a supplied drug formulation on a consistent active-moiety basis. This is a concentration definition without patient-population calibration or administration advice.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; not merely solvent volume added before dissolution.

variables.definition: Mass of one identified constituent divided by total final solution volume.
variables.context: Same identified active constituent and homogeneous liquid formulation sample, final sample volume, temperature and composition state. Clinical application is a supplied drug formulation on a consistent active-moiety basis. This is a concentration definition without patient-population calibration or administration advice.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; active-moiety definition, phase and formulation conditions must be specified.

assumptions: Source definition: the medical arithmetic workbook explicitly gives C=D/V for drug mass and solution volume.
Application profile: one homogeneous liquid formulation, defined constituent/active moiety and final volume. No clinical age, pregnancy or disease validation is supplied by a concentration identity.
limitations: Bulk density, mass fraction, molarity and pharmacological potency are distinct quantities; no unit-only substitution is authorized.
Does not establish solubility, stability, product identity or whether a formulation is suitable for a patient. Reconstitution diluent volume may differ from final volume.

models.inverse_notes: Target m: known C>=0,V>0 give m=C*V uniquely. Check C=25 kg/m^3,V=5e-6 m^3 gives m=0.000125 kg and forward C=25. C=0 gives m=0 uniquely. Target V: known m>0,C>0 give V=m/C>0. With m=C=0, every V>0 fits, so V is not identified; m>0 with C=0 has no finite positive-volume solution; m=0,C>0 would require V=0 and is excluded. Retain original constituent/final-volume context; inversion does not authorize a formulation change.

models.title: Mass concentration after solute-conserving dilution
models.summary: Maps initial concentration and aliquot volume to final concentration when only solute-free diluent is added and the selected solute mass is conserved. It does not choose a drug, dilution target or preparation procedure.

relationship.original_equation: C1 V1 = C2 V2 for unchanged solute amount during dilution
relationship.locator: Chemistry 2e, section 3.3 Molarity, Dilution of Solutions, general concentration-volume form and unchanged-solute explanation
relationship.translation_notes: Source general C and V notation is preserved with initial/final subscripts serialized as C1,V1,C2,V2. Source explains conservation for amount concentration and explicitly allows other mutually consistent concentration/volume units. This record uses mass concentration of one conserved solute; C1*V1 and C2*V2 are its mass. Both C values are kg/m^3 and volumes are m^3, so C2 is kg/m^3 and the runtime mass scale cancels consistently. Dimensions: (M L^-3)*L^3/L^3=M L^-3. No assumption of additive solution volumes is needed because V2 is the final supplied volume. V2>=V1 declares the dilution/no-change profile, excluding concentration by evaporation. Unlike the b02 desired-over-have definition, two states of one conserved solute are related here; no independent prescription amount is a port.

variables.definition: Mass concentration of the identified conserved solute in the starting aliquot.
variables.context: Same identified conserved solute/active moiety, initial liquid aliquot and final diluted liquid mixture at specified conditions. Final volume is supplied as a final measured/defined value, not assumed from additive ingredient volumes. Clinical use requires an independently authorized compatible diluent/formulation; no patient-population calibration is claimed.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative. Zero is the blank-solute limit; no solute is introduced by the diluent.

variables.definition: Positive volume of the initial homogeneous aliquot actually transferred into the dilution.
variables.context: Same identified conserved solute/active moiety, initial liquid aliquot and final diluted liquid mixture at specified conditions. Final volume is supplied as a final measured/defined value, not assumed from additive ingredient volumes. Clinical use requires an independently authorized compatible diluent/formulation; no patient-population calibration is claimed.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; not total bottle volume if only an aliquot is transferred.

variables.definition: Total final diluted formulation volume after mixing, supplied independently.
variables.context: Same identified conserved solute/active moiety, initial liquid aliquot and final diluted liquid mixture at specified conditions. Final volume is supplied as a final measured/defined value, not assumed from additive ingredient volumes. Clinical use requires an independently authorized compatible diluent/formulation; no patient-population calibration is claimed.
variables.domain: Finite and at least V1; positive follows from V1>0. Equality is the no-dilution identity boundary.

variables.definition: Mass concentration of the same conserved solute in the final homogeneous mixture.
variables.context: Same identified conserved solute/active moiety, initial liquid aliquot and final diluted liquid mixture at specified conditions. Final volume is supplied as a final measured/defined value, not assumed from additive ingredient volumes. Clinical use requires an independently authorized compatible diluent/formulation; no patient-population calibration is claimed.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative and no greater than C1 in the declared dilution profile.

assumptions: Source assumption: dilution preserves the chosen solute amount; its concentration-volume products are equal before and after adding solute-free solvent.
Application profile: selected solute is neither added, lost, reacted, precipitated nor selectively adsorbed; the initial aliquot and final mixture are homogeneous on the specified sampling supports.
Clinical profile: authorized compatible formulation and final volume are external; this is conservation arithmetic without a therapeutic validation population.
limitations: Not applicable to adding another active-solute solution, chemical conversion, losses, incomplete transfer or a concentration-by-solvent-removal process.
Does not calculate final volume by adding solvent and solution volumes; no drug compatibility, stability, sterility or preparation recommendation follows.

models.inverse_notes: Target C1: known C2>=0,V1>0,V2>=V1 give C1=C2*V2/V1 uniquely; C2=0 gives C1=0. Target V1: C1>0,C2>0,V2>0 give V1=C2*V2/C1 and require V1<=V2. With C1=C2=0, any positive volumes satisfying V2>=V1 fit; neither volume is identified. One zero concentration and the other positive has no solution with finite positive volumes. Retain original conservation/context assumptions in every direction; do not infer clinical preparation authorization.

models.title: Infused drug mass rate from concentration and fluid flow
models.summary: Concentration times volumetric flow gives the selected constituent's mass delivery rate at the same boundary. This single transport relationship is distinct from a composed weight-to-pump dosing scenario.

relationship.original_equation: Infusion mass rate = concentration x infusion flow rate
relationship.locator: Topic 1, 3a Infusions, printed page20 (PDF index19), main displayed relation and 10 mg/mL, 1 mL/min example
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced q maps to the source infusion flow rate (also V in its example); introduced r maps to source infusion mass rate, while C remains concentration. Use C in kg/m^3, q in m^3/s and r in kg/s. Dimensions: (M L^-3)*(L^3 T^-1)=M T^-1. The kg mass scale appears equally in C and r, so expression C*q is canonical without a mg/min or hour conversion literal. For fixed C, the relation also connects interval means exactly because constituent mass in every fluid portion is proportional to volume. That temporal interpretation is an explicit source-backed constant-concentration extension, not a claim about varying C. No weight-based amount, drug-selection rule or concentration-to-dose chain is built into this atomic transport relationship.

variables.definition: Mass concentration of the selected active constituent in the infused homogeneous solution.
variables.context: Same identified active drug/moiety, homogeneous infusion solution, delivery boundary and interval. Concentration is constant; q and r are interval means, also instantaneous values only for a constant-rate application. Rates/formulation are supplied for qualified arithmetic; source is medical education without a drug-specific patient validation population.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative and constant over the interval at the delivery boundary; zero is a blank-carrier limit, not a drug recommendation.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced q maps to infusion flow rate; source example also calls it V
variables.definition: Nonnegative fluid volume delivered per elapsed time at the same boundary and interval.
variables.context: Same identified active drug/moiety, homogeneous infusion solution, delivery boundary and interval. Concentration is constant; q and r are interval means, also instantaneous values only for a constant-rate application. Rates/formulation are supplied for qualified arithmetic; source is medical education without a drug-specific patient validation population.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; zero denotes no flow. Constant rate is needed only to identify the mean with a fixed instantaneous setting.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced r maps to Infusion mass rate
variables.definition: Mass of the selected active constituent delivered per elapsed time at the specified boundary.
variables.context: Same identified active drug/moiety, homogeneous infusion solution, delivery boundary and interval. Concentration is constant; q and r are interval means, also instantaneous values only for a constant-rate application. Rates/formulation are supplied for qualified arithmetic; source is medical education without a drug-specific patient validation population.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; delivered at boundary, not absorbed amount, systemic concentration or effect.

assumptions: Source relationship: medical workbook distinguishes fluid volume flow from constituent mass flow and multiplies concentration by volumetric rate.

Application profile: selected-constituent concentration is homogeneous and constant; rates use the same time aggregation and boundary. No patient-specific clinical validation is asserted by this transport identity.
limitations: If concentration varies in time, a product of separate interval means is generally insufficient; a matched integral or aligned subinterval model is required.
Does not include drug absorption, distribution, clearance, pump accuracy, line dead volume or therapeutic suitability. No dose or flow setting is recommended.

models.inverse_notes: Target q: known r>=0,C>0 give q=r/C uniquely; target C: known r>=0,q>0 give C=r/q uniquely. Retain source concentration, boundary and temporal assumptions. Check r=1.6666666666666668e-7 kg/s,C=10 kg/m^3 gives q=1.6666666666666667e-8 m^3/s and forward r matches. r=0,C>0 gives q=0; r=0,q>0 gives C=0, both admitted arithmetic boundaries. When C=r=0, any q>=0 fits; when q=r=0, any C>=0 fits. A positive r with a zero known multiplier has no solution. Algebraic inversion does not authorize choosing a clinical flow or formulation.

models.title: Signed postpartum body-mass retention relative to a baseline
models.summary: Postpartum mass minus early- or pre-pregnancy baseline mass. Positive values mean retained mass relative to that baseline; negative values remain signed differences rather than being clamped to zero.

relationship.original_equation: Postpartum weight retention is the difference between body weight at a given postpartum time and early- or pre-pregnancy body weight
relationship.locator: Chapter 13 Glossary, Postpartum weight retention, printed p165 (PDF index164)
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced wp,w0,delta map to source postpartum body weight, early/pre-pregnancy weight and their difference. Use actual mass in kg rather than force; dimensions M-M=M. The expression remains unchanged in the snapshot mass base because all three mass quantities share the kg unit scale. No percentage or elapsed-time rate is computed. A specified baseline is essential: early-pregnancy and pre-pregnancy measurements cannot silently be pooled. The source prose says difference; retain its signed mathematical meaning rather than creating a nonnegative-only profile. The report focuses on pregnancy and up to 24 months after delivery; the glossary definition supplies no fitted time coefficient or universal clinical cutoff.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced wp maps to body weight at a given time postpartum
variables.definition: Actual body mass at the identified postpartum assessment following the specified childbirth event.
variables.context: Same person following a childbirth event, body mass at a specified postpartum assessment and an explicitly identified pre-pregnancy or early-pregnancy baseline. Both are actual measured body masses on comparable measurement bases. Source glossary is in a maternal nutrition report; the difference is definitional, not a calibrated clinical risk or treatment model.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive measured body mass; assessment timing recorded externally.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced w0 maps to early or pre-pregnancy body weight

variables.context: Same person following a childbirth event, body mass at a specified postpartum assessment and an explicitly identified pre-pregnancy or early-pregnancy baseline. Both are actual measured body masses on comparable measurement bases. Source glossary is in a maternal nutrition report; the difference is definitional, not a calibrated clinical risk or treatment model.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced delta maps to Postpartum weight retention
variables.definition: Signed postpartum mass difference relative to the specified baseline.
variables.context: Same person following a childbirth event, body mass at a specified postpartum assessment and an explicitly identified pre-pregnancy or early-pregnancy baseline. Both are actual measured body masses on comparable measurement bases. Source glossary is in a maternal nutrition report; the difference is definitional, not a calibrated clinical risk or treatment model.
variables.domain: Finite real, including zero and negative values. Sign describes arithmetic relative mass only.

assumptions: Source definition: the SACN glossary compares body weight at a specified postpartum time with early- or pre-pregnancy weight.

Application profile: same person/pregnancy, explicit baseline type and comparable measurement conditions. The source report concerns girls/women of childbearing age and maternal outcomes; no age-specific prediction validity or new physiological relationship is claimed.
This is a signed mass-accounting definition without diagnosis, treatment selection or monitoring instructions.
limitations: Does not separate fat, lean mass, fluid changes or effects of measurement timing; it is not a body-fat or energy-balance estimate.
No missing baseline imputation, recommended weight trajectory, pregnancy treatment or clinical risk threshold is supplied. Different baseline types are not interchangeable.

references.method: Independent synthetic difference check: adding five whole kg and one half kg to 64 kg reaches 69.5 kg, hence signed retention is +5.5 kg. Tolerance is floating arithmetic only.
references.provenance: Curator-created mass-difference example, not observed maternal data.

references.method: Independent signed subtraction: current mass is three kg below the declared baseline, so the difference is -3 kg. This rejects silent clamping while retaining two positive body masses.
Identical positive body masses have zero difference; this is an admissible equality boundary, not a zero-mass body.

rejection_cases.reason: A zero-body-mass baseline is not admissible.
Baseline mass is missing; it cannot be inferred from postpartum mass.

models.inverse_notes: Target wp: known delta and w0>0 give wp=delta+w0, with wp>0 requiring delta>-w0. Target w0: known wp>0 and delta give w0=wp-delta, with w0>0 requiring delta<wp. No denominators or multiple roots occur. Check delta=5.5,w0=64 gives wp=69.5 kg and forward delta=5.5; delta=-3,w0=60 gives wp=57 and forward -3. At delta=0, each known positive mass uniquely determines the equal other mass, so there is no zero-difference ambiguity when one mass is known. Without either mass, delta alone leaves infinitely many pairs. Retain same-pregnancy baseline context; inversion is accounting rather than causation.

gaps: Need postpartum_body_mass_retention meaning; body_mass and kg already exist. Source-specific time and baseline contexts must remain explicit. No runtime projection.
